Account.doc: One account in the chart of accounts.

fields.name: account_type
fields.doc: One of `ACCOUNT_TYPES`.

fields.name: default_tax_rate_id
fields.doc: The tax rate a new line coded to this account starts with.

fields.name: class
fields.doc: asset, liability, equity, revenue or expense — derived from the type.

fields.name: system
fields.doc: AR, AP, sales tax and retained earnings: the ledger needs them.

fields.name: balance
fields.doc: All-time ledger balance, debit positive.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: `sales` (aged receivables) or `bill` (aged payables).

fields.name: current
fields.doc: Not yet due.

Approval.doc: An approved invoice or bill, frozen at the moment of approval.

fields.name: balance
fields.doc: The ledger's balance for the account.

fields.name: statement_balance
fields.doc: The sum of every imported statement line.

BankTransaction.doc:
Spend money or receive money: a bank movement coded straight to accounts,
with no invoice behind it (bank fees, a card purchase, interest received).

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: `spend` or `receive`.

Contact.doc: A customer, a supplier, or both — which one is derived from the documents.

fields.name: receivable
fields.doc: Outstanding on approved sales invoices: what they owe you.

fields.name: payable
fields.doc: Outstanding on approved bills: what you owe them.

fields.name: profit_ytd
fields.doc: Net profit for the financial year to `today`.

HistoryEntry.doc:
One entry in a record's audit trail, or a note on it. `Authored`: the author
is the owner stamp, and nobody else can rewrite or remove it.

Invoice.doc:
A sales invoice or a bill while it is a DRAFT. Approving it freezes a copy
into `approvals`, and from then on the ledger reads that copy, never this
row — so an edit to these registers after approval (which honest nodes
refuse, and a patched node could still write) changes nothing posted.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: `sales` or `bill`. Fixed at creation.

fields.name: lines
fields.doc:
The lines as one value: a draft is edited as a whole form, and two
people re-ordering one invoice's lines should not interleave them.

fields.name: notes
fields.doc: Terms or a note printed on the invoice.

InvoiceDetail.doc: An invoice with its payments and audit trail (named struct, never a tuple).

fields.name: number
fields.doc:
`INV-0007` for an approved sales invoice: its position among approved
sales invoices, derived on read. Empty for drafts and bills (a bill's
number is the supplier's, in `reference`).

fields.name: status
fields.doc:
draft, awaiting_payment, paid or void. Overdue is the reader's call:
it depends on today.

fields.name: conflicted
fields.doc:
More than one member filed an approval for this invoice. Only possible
from a patched node; the earliest is used and the UI says so.

Journal.doc: A manual journal — and a bank transfer, which is a two-line journal.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: `journal` or `transfer`.

fields.name: balanced
fields.doc:
False for a journal that does not balance — only a patched node can
write one. It is left out of the ledger and shown so someone voids it.

fields.name: balance
fields.doc: Running balance, debit positive.

Line.doc:
A stored document line. `tax_bp` is the rate captured when the line was
saved, so changing a tax rate later never rewrites a posted document.

fields.name: quantity
fields.doc: Thousandths of a unit.

fields.name: unit_price
fields.doc: Minor units per whole unit. Negative for a discount line.

LineInput.doc:
A document line as the form sends it. The tax rate is captured from
`tax_rate_id` on save.

fields.name: history
fields.doc: Audit trail and notes, per record. Each entry is its author's.

fields.name: month
fields.doc: `YYYY-MM`.

Payment.doc: Money received against an invoice, or paid against a bill.

fields.name: amount
fields.doc: Always positive; the direction comes from the invoice's kind.

fields.name: fy_end_month
fields.doc: The month the financial year ends in, 1..=12.

fields.name: tax_label
fields.doc: What tax is called here: Tax, VAT, GST, Sales Tax.

fields.name: lock_date
fields.doc: Nothing dated on or before it can be posted or voided.

StatementLine.doc:
One line of a bank statement, imported from the bank's CSV.

The id is a hash of the line's content (see `statement_line_id`), so two
members importing the same file produce the same rows rather than two
copies, and re-importing an overlapping file adds only the new lines.

fields.name: amount
fields.doc: Signed: money in is positive, money out negative.

fields.name: matched
fields.doc:
The payment or bank transaction it is reconciled against. Whether the
line counts as reconciled is derived on read: the target must exist,
be live, sit in the same bank account and move the same amount.

fields.name: match_label
fields.doc: What it is matched to, for the reconcile screen ("INV-0003 · Acme").

fields.name: rate_bp
fields.doc: Basis points: 2000 is 20%.

fields.name: net_tax
fields.doc: Positive: owed to the tax authority. Negative: a refund is due.

VoidRecord.doc:
A void: the reversal of a posted record. Any member's void voids it; there
is no un-void, exactly as on paper.

methods.name: account_transactions
methods.doc:
One account's general ledger for a period, with opening and closing
balances and a running balance on every row.

methods.name: approve_invoice
methods.doc:
Approve a draft: freeze it into a write-once approval and post it to the
ledger. A sales invoice gets its number here.

methods.name: code_statement_line
methods.doc:
Reconcile a line by creating what it records: spend money for money
out, receive money for money in, coded to one account, the statement
amount taken as tax-inclusive. Returns the new transaction's id.

methods.name: create_bank_transaction
methods.doc:
Spend money (`kind` = `spend`) or receive money (`receive`) straight
through a bank account, coded to accounts with no invoice behind it.

methods.name: create_invoice
methods.doc: Save a new draft invoice (`kind` = `sales`) or bill (`kind` = `bill`).

methods.name: create_journal
methods.doc:
Post a manual journal. Its lines must balance — debits equal credits —
and a journal that does not is left out of the ledger even if a patched
node writes one.

methods.name: delete_account
methods.doc:
Delete an account nothing has ever been coded to. One with history is
archived instead: the ledger has to keep naming it.

methods.name: delete_contact
methods.doc:
Delete a contact no document names. One with documents stays: the
ledger and the audit trail have to keep naming them.

methods.name: delete_invoice
methods.doc: Delete a draft. An approved document is voided instead, never deleted.

methods.name: delete_statement_line
methods.doc: Remove an unreconciled statement line (a bad import).

methods.name: get_dashboard
methods.doc:
The home screen: bank balances, what is owed each way, six months of
cash in and out, and profit for the year to `today` (`YYYY-MM-DD`,
supplied by the caller so the read is a pure function of state).

methods.name: import_statement_lines
methods.doc:
Import statement lines into a bank account. Lines already imported (by
anyone) are skipped, so an overlapping export is safe to import again.
Returns how many lines were new.

methods.name: list_accounts
methods.doc: The chart, by code, each account with its all-time ledger balance.

methods.name: list_contacts
methods.doc: Everyone in the address book, by name, with what they owe and are owed.

methods.name: list_history
methods.doc: A record's audit trail and notes, oldest first, each with its author.

methods.name: list_invoices
methods.doc:
Sales invoices and/or bills (`kind` = `sales` | `bill` | none for both),
newest issue date first.

methods.name: list_payments
methods.doc: Payments, optionally through one bank account, newest first.

methods.name: list_statement_lines
methods.doc:
A bank account's statement lines, newest first, each with whether it is
reconciled (derived: its match must be live and move the same amount).

methods.name: reconcile_statement_line
methods.doc:
Match a statement line to the payment, bank transaction or transfer it
records. The target must move the same amount through the same account,
and must not already be matched to another line.

methods.name: record_payment
methods.doc:
Record money received against an invoice, or paid against a bill.
Refused beyond the amount due.

methods.name: record_transfer
methods.doc: Move money between two bank accounts: a two-line journal.

methods.name: set_account_archived
methods.doc: Archive an account (hide it from pickers, keep its history) or restore it.

methods.name: set_lock_date
methods.doc:
Lock the ledger up to and including a date (a filed tax period, a closed
year), or unlock them with `None`. Honest nodes refuse to post or void
anything dated on or before it.

methods.name: update_invoice
methods.doc:
Edit a draft. Only fields whose value differs are written, so a
teammate's concurrent edit to another field survives. Refused once the
document is approved: from then on it is posted.

methods.name: update_tax_rate
methods.doc: Rename or re-rate. Posted documents keep the rate they were saved with.

methods.name: void_record
methods.doc:
Void a posted record: an approved invoice or bill, a payment, a bank
transaction or a journal. Its entries leave the ledger; the record and
its void stay, attributed, for the audit trail. There is no un-void.

events.name: BankTransactionRecorded
events.doc: Spend money or receive money was recorded.

events.name: ContactChanged
events.doc: A contact was added, edited or removed.

events.name: InvoiceApproved
events.doc: An invoice or bill was approved and posted to the ledger.

events.name: InvoiceSaved
events.doc: A draft invoice or bill was created or edited.

events.name: JournalPosted
events.doc: A manual journal or a transfer was posted.

events.name: NoteAdded
events.doc: A note was added to a record.

events.name: PaymentRecorded
events.doc: A payment was recorded against an invoice or bill.

events.name: SettingsChanged
events.doc: Organisation settings or the lock date changed.

events.name: StatementChanged
events.doc: Statement lines were imported, reconciled, unreconciled or removed.
